messages:
Olivia: hi everyone  first week, small demo question. i created a hosted API key via the console but when i run 4 concurrent streaming clients i hit 429s. should i be using a sandbox key instead for demos?
Ravi: welcome Olivia! hosted keys are fine but quotas depend on your org plan. sandbox is shared and usually more restrictive. 4 concurrent streams can hit a concurrent-streams cap or a tokens/min bucket depending on prompt size.
Olivia: how do i check which quota i'm tripping? the client just shows 429.
Devex: check the HTTP response headers and the JSON body on the 429. we include a reason string and reset info. example: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 1900004380
x-rw-retry-after: 1.7
{ "error": "rate_limited", "reason": "concurrent_streams" }
```
Ravi: common reasons you'll see: concurrent_streams, requests_per_min, tokens_per_min. embeddings sometimes have separate counters; look for x-rw-embed-* headers.
Kai: practical tip: for browser demos, multiplex logical conversations over a single streaming connection instead of opening N websockets. tag each message with a lightweight session_id. that keeps the active connection count low.
Olivia: is multiplexing supported by Redwood SDKs or do i need to roll my own?
Ravi: SDKs don't enforce a multiplex protocol by default, but it's straightforward: open one stream, prefix messages with session_id, route server-side. we have internal examples in the devex playbook.
Devex: if you need an easier route, ping #devex for a temporary sandbox bump or a dedicated demo key. we can often enable a 24-48h boost for onboarding demos if you provide the window and concurrent connections estimate. RateBot: devex-boost-request queued (ID: RB-2201).
Olivia: are ephemeral CI tokens different? i'm using ephemeral tokens in a small runner and wondered if they bypass limits.
Kai: ephemeral tokens inherit the quotas of the org/project they belong to. they don't bypass rate limits. if CI is noisy, ask devex for a dedicated demo key or reduce CI parallelism.
Olivia: embeddings vs chat  do those consume the same quota? my demo mixes both.
Ravi: many orgs count embeddings against tokens/min too, but some plans have separated embedding quotas. check response headers for embedding counters; if none, assume shared.
Olivia: any quick backoff pattern for streaming 429s?
Kai: for connection-level 429s, reconnect with exp backoff + jitter: base ~250ms, max ~5s, cap attempts ~6. avoid hot-loop reconnecting. for request-level 429s, stagger retries per logical session so you don't retry all at once.
Olivia: perfect. i'll try multiplexing and ping #devex if needed. thanks! :smile:
Ravi: welcome again — feel free to DM if you want help wiring multiplexing or sharing the demo window so devex can pre-authorize.
Devex: closing note: when you file a boost request include (1) username/email, (2) demo window in UTC, (3) estimated concurrent streams, and (4) whether embeddings are used. that helps us approve quickly.
